Functional evolution of EGLN1 / PHD2 in the guinea pig

Phylogenomics + protein-language-model analysis · query: Cavia porcellus EGLN1 (RefSeq XP_013011725.3, 388 aa) · reference: human PHD2 (UniProt Q9GZT9, 426 aa)

Bottom line for the enhancement hypothesis. The catalytic core of PHD2 is absolutely conserved in guinea pig — so if EGLN1 contributes to guinea-pig hypoxia tolerance, it is not through the active site. Re-scoring all 22 guinea-pig-specific substitutions on a directional (gain-of-function) axis identifies I259V as the strongest enhancement/stabilizing candidate: a second-shell substitution near the 2-oxoglutarate pocket that our ancestral reconstruction shows is an evolutionary reversion to the deep-ancestral valine — lost in placental mammals and re-acquired in the guinea-pig clade.

1. Question and approach

EGLN1 encodes PHD2, the principal cellular oxygen sensor: a 2-oxoglutarate/Fe(II)-dependent prolyl-4-hydroxylase that hydroxylates HIF-1α, tagging it for degradation. Under hypoxia PHD2 slows, HIF stabilizes, and the hypoxia transcriptional program switches on. Variants that re-tune PHD2 activity are a recurring theme in human high-altitude adaptation, so the guinea pig — a hystricomorph rodent with a high-altitude Andean origin — is a natural place to look for functional EGLN1 substitutions.

Workflow: (1) assemble full-length EGLN1 orthologs across a two-tier taxon set (dense mammals + a thin deep backbone), (2) align and build a phylogeny, (3) map the catalytic residues and trace their evolution by ancestral-sequence reconstruction (ASR), (4) enumerate guinea-pig-specific substitutions, (5) score each with four independent methods and rank them by direction of effect, and (6) characterize the top candidates structurally and mechanistically.

Scope note. Strict 1:1 EGLN1 orthology is eukaryotic. The deepest nodes in the tree are anchored by the shared 2-OG/Fe(II) oxygenase catalytic fold (homology), not by one-to-one orthology. "All domains of life" is therefore represented at the level of the catalytic machinery; the fine-grained lineage analysis is within Metazoa.

2. Phylogeny of EGLN1

54 full-length sequences (42 mammals + 12 deep-backbone metazoans; RefSeq, length range 127–723 aa) were aligned with MAFFT L-INS-i and trimmed, and a maximum-likelihood tree inferred with IQ-TREE (best model JTT+G4, 1000 ultrafast-bootstrap replicates, rooted on the invertebrate outgroup). The topology is biologically correct: guinea pig sits inside a monophyletic Hystricomorpha (with chinchilla, degu, naked mole-rat), nested within monophyletic Rodentia; deep nodes are well supported.

Figure 1. Maximum-likelihood phylogeny of EGLN1 across 54 taxa. Guinea pig in red; clades colored; ultrafast-bootstrap support on deep nodes. Guinea-pig terminal branch length 0.020.

3. The catalytic core is invariant — including in guinea pig

The five catalytic residues of human PHD2 — the Fe(II)-coordinating triad His313 / Asp315 / His374 and the 2-OG-binding Tyr329 / Arg383 — were mapped onto the alignment and reconstructed at every ancestral node.

ResidueRoleConservation (54 taxa)Guinea pigASR posterior (Bilaterian→Hystrico)

Every catalytic residue reconstructs at posterior probability 1.00 from the Bilaterian root through the Hystricomorpha ancestor to guinea pig — the machinery has been invariant for ~600 Myr, and guinea pig retains the full ancestral catalytic state.

Figure 2. Per-residue conservation across PHD2. Catalytic residues (▽) are perfectly conserved; guinea-pig substitutions (dots) all fall away from the active site — the nearest is 14.8 Å (Cα–2-OG) from the cofactor.

Interpretation. A guinea-pig EGLN1 functional change cannot be a catalytic-site substitution — there are none. Any functional effect must act through the second shell, dynamics, stability, or regulatory regions.

4. Guinea-pig-specific substitutions and directional scoring

22 substitutions distinguish guinea-pig EGLN1 from the mammalian consensus (differ from the consensus over 42 mammals, ≤10% shared, all derived relative to the placental ancestor). 4 lie in the catalytic domain (all second-shell), 18 in the N-terminal MYND/Zn-finger and linker region.

4.1 Why the ranking was re-oriented toward enhancement

Standard language-model log-likelihood ratios (LLR = log P(mutant) − log P(WT)) measure the magnitude of a perturbation, not its direction. For a gain-of-function hypothesis that is the wrong axis. We therefore used the structure-conditioned ProteinMPNN log-odds as a zero-shot ΔΔG proxy (the basis of ThermoMPNN-style stability prediction): a positive value means the folded structure favors the guinea-pig residue (stabilizing, enhancement-compatible); negative means destabilizing (loss-of-function-like). ProteinMPNN was run on the full-length human AlphaFold model to score all 22 positions on this directional axis, cross-checked against the crystal structure for the four catalytic-domain sites (I259V +2.6/+3.2, K291M −3.3/−2.9 — consistent).

Figure 3. Directional effect of each guinea-pig substitution. Left: structure-conditioned ΔΔG proxy — bars to the right (green) are stabilizing/enhancement-compatible; to the left (red) are loss-of-function-like. Right: enhancement quadrant (upper-right) — structure favors the residue and the sequence LMs find it plausible; marker size ∝ evolutionary conservation. I259V is the clear outlier.

4.2 Four-method comparison

Each substitution was scored by ESM-2 (650M) masked-marginal LLR, ESMC-300M masked-marginal LLR, ProteinMPNN structure-conditioned log-odds, and an MSA log-odds conservation baseline. The methods agree on direction for the strong cases: I259V is favored by every structure-aware method; K291M, P85V and G66K are destabilizing across the board.

5.1 I259V — the standout (evolutionary reversion, structure-stabilizing)

Ile259 is buried in the β-sheet core of the catalytic domain, ~15 Å from the 2-oxoglutarate cofactor (a true second-shell position). Isoleucine → valine removes a single Cδ methyl group. In this tightly packed environment (neighbours Trp258, Val300) that relieves steric over-packing, which ProteinMPNN scores as strongly stabilizing (ΔΔG proxy +3.25) and ESMC independently favors (+3.07). Crucially, ASR shows this is a reversion: the deep ancestor (Bilaterian root, tetrapods) is reconstructed as valine, placental mammals switched to isoleucine (posterior 1.0), and the guinea-pig clade reverted to valine. The deep-node valine assignments carry only moderate support (Tetrapod V = 0.57, Bilaterian V = 0.62), but the functionally decisive mammal→Hystricomorpha Ile→Val switch is reconstructed with certainty.

5.2 G223S — active-site-flanking helix rigidification

Gly223 lies in a helix turn near the substrate channel (~14 Å from 2-OG). Glycine → serine removes a helix-destabilizing glycine and adds a hydroxyl H-bond donor — both helix-stabilizing. This is a guinea-pig terminal-branch change (Gly conserved through the Hystricomorpha ancestor).

Figure 4. Structural characterization of the two crystal-resolved enhancement candidates on the PHD2 catalytic domain (PDB 5L9B). (A) Overview with Fe site and 2-OG. (B,C) Ile259→Val259: loss of the Cδ methyl in the packed core. (D,E) Gly223→Ser223: added hydroxyl in an active-site-flanking helix. (F) Predicted mechanisms.

Figure 5. Ancestral-sequence reconstruction at the five enhancement positions along the guinea-pig lineage (green = guinea-pig residue present). I259V is a reversion to the deep-ancestral valine; G9S and N161L are Hystricomorpha-ancestor innovations; G223S and D171V are recent Cavia-specific changes. Per-cell posteriors are shown where <1.0; the mammalian and Hystricomorpha states are near-certain (≈1.0), whereas the deepest (Bilaterian/Tetrapod) states — flagged with dashed red borders — carry lower support (posterior 0.11–0.62). The reversion inference for I259V rests on the Tetrapod (V, 0.57) and Bilaterian (V, 0.62) reconstructions plus the certain mammal→Hystricomorpha switch, so the ML topology of the reversion is robust even though the deep-node confidence is moderate.

Confidence caveat. I259V and G223S are resolved in the PHD2 crystal structure and their mechanisms are structurally grounded. N161L, G9S and D171V lie in the N-terminal/linker region, which is modeled only at low AlphaFold confidence (pLDDT 38–59) and is disordered in all crystal structures — their structure-based scores should be treated as provisional. Notably, the two known human adaptive sites (D4E, C127S) are also N-terminal, so this region is not without adaptive precedent.

6. Interpretation in the high-altitude context

Whether an adaptive PHD2 change should increase or decrease activity is genuinely debated even for the best-studied human variant. The Tibetan PHD2 D4E/C127S allele has been characterized as a gain-of-function variant with increased hydroxylase activity and lower Km (more active at low O₂), associated with the blunted-erythropoiesis phenotype that protects Tibetans from chronic mountain sickness; other work argues the same allele is loss-of-function via defective p23-cochaperone binding. We therefore report direction with mechanism rather than forcing a single label.

For the guinea pig, the pattern that emerges is consistent and specific: the catalytic core is untouchable, and the strongest signal is a structure-stabilizing, second-shell, evolutionarily-reverted substitution (I259V) positioned to fine-tune the 2-OG pocket environment. That is exactly the molecular signature expected of an activity-tuning rather than activity-abolishing change — the enhancement direction your hypothesis predicts.

Recommended experimental test. Express human PHD2 and the I259V variant, and measure hydroxylase kinetics (kcat, Km for 2-OG and for the HIF-1α CODD peptide) under a range of O₂ tensions. The prediction is that I259V is thermostabilizing and increases activity or lowers Km — testable by thermal-shift and in-vitro hydroxylation assays. G223S is the natural second target.

7. Methods summary

  • Sequences: full-length EGLN1 from NCBI RefSeq (Ensembl returned fragments); guinea-pig query XP_013011725.3 (isoform X1, 388 aa); human reference Q9GZT9 (426 aa). 54 taxa total.
  • Alignment: MAFFT L-INS-i; trimAl. Tree: IQ-TREE, JTT+G4, 1000 UFBoot, rooted on invertebrate outgroup.
  • ASR: IQ-TREE empirical-Bayes marginal reconstruction (JTT+G4) on the rooted topology.
  • Scoring: ESM-2 650M and ESMC-300M masked-marginal LLR (all 22 muts); ProteinMPNN v_48_020 structure-conditioned log-odds on the 5L9B crystal (4 catalytic-domain muts) and the full-length human AlphaFold model (all 22, as ΔΔG proxy); MSA log-odds baseline. Scoring in the human sequence/structure background.
  • Structures: PHD2 crystal 5L9B (Mn + 2-OG); PyMOL mutagenesis for WT→variant renders. AlphaFold model AF-Q9GZT9-F1 (v6) for N-terminal positions.
